newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-LIPTON CHAMPIONSHIPS LOCKER ROOM DEDICATED TO GULLIKSON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-LIPTON CHAMPIONSHIPS LOCKER ROOM DEDICATED TO GULLIKSON.

text.p: The men's locker room at the Lipton Championships was formally dedicated to Tim Gullikson, the former tour player and coach of Pete Sampras who died last May.
World number one Sampras and Gullikson's wife, Rosemary, were present for the Saturday ceremony to unveil a plaque in the locker room honouring Gullikson's memory.

Inscriped on the plaque: "To Tim, who treated a locker room as his living room on the road - a place to meet and greet friends, offer moral support to, and enjoy the camaraderie of, his fellow tennis players."
Sampras and Rosemary Gullikson both felt it a fitting tribute to the popular player and coach, who died of brain tumours at the age of 44.

"Tim never got injured, but he spent more time in the locker room than anyone. He loved hanging out with the boys, watching the girls' matches, giving those girls a hard time," recalled Sampras, who reached the top of the tennis world under Gullikson's guidance.
"I'm sure he's looking down today and happy because he would have loved it," Sampras said of this particular tribute.
"I spent many, many hours during Tim's 20 years on the tour waiting for him to come out of the locker room," Rosemary Gullikson said.
"He went there for the sheer pleasure of the company he enjoyed with the players and his friends, so this is totally fitting. I know he'd love this."
